**Job Description

_Would you like to use your property management experience to help develop solutions that create real value? As a Property Manager at Netcompany, you will work with technical teams and customers to turn real-life experience into solutions that improve property management through a data driven approach that ensure the right usage of AI and digital capabilities.

_

**Responsibilities

**

Netcompany is looking for a Property Manager to take a key role in the continued development of our property management solutions. The role is for an experienced, operational property manager who knows the reality of managing properties day to day and can use that experience to help shape better digital solutions. You will bring hands-on knowledge of property management into the product development process and work closely with technical and refinement teams to ensure that solutions reflect real-life processes, challenges and user needs. You will also contribute to customer dialogue, where your practical experience helps create credibility and a strong understanding of how the product can support customers in their daily work.

A significant part of the role involves leveraging your property management experience in product improvements, customer insight and relevant market activities. You will participate in customer meetings, support pre-sales activities and contribute to business development through market dialogue and feedback from existing and potential customers. This is not a sales role; your contribution is your professional expertise and ability to understand the customer's operational reality, ask the right questions and help connect their needs with the capabilities of the product.

**Your responsibilites will typically include:

**

• Ensuring the product delivers value, automation potential and efficiency across the property management value chain

• Working closely with the technical team and refinement team on product development

• Supporting business development and sales activities through market dialogue, customer feedback and pre-sales activities

• Participating in customer meetings and other client-facing activities

• Building trust and credibility in customer dialogues

**About you

**

To succeed in this role, you:

• Have solid operational experience working as a property manager

• Contribute with operational experience across a property portfolio, including the full complexity of Danish regulatory requirements (eg. cost control rent 'OMK', free market rent, taxes, duties and rates, operational budgets)

• Have experience across residential, commercial and mixed properties including the customer reporting requirements a property manager faces

• Have experience as a power user or super user of a property management software system

• Have full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken) is a must.

**Continue developing with us

**

At Netcompany, we focus on your personal and professional development.

We provide a structured career model that allows you to build on your existing experiences.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will support your development and help you achieve your personal and professional goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague in management gives you concrete insights into the various business areas and responsibilities that match your interests and desires.

Additionally, you will be enrolled in our internal training programme, Netcompany Academy, where you are offered courses and seminars tailored to you and where you are in your career. All courses are taught by experienced Netcompany colleagues, ensuring that all content is highly relevant and builds upon your professional skills. Participating alongside colleagues from across the company helps you build a solid network and provides a strong foundation for your career at Netcompany, both professionally and socially.

Join an inclusive community

At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand your network.

**Send us an application

**

Upload your resume and a motivational letter to our recruitment system via the link. If you have unanswered questions, feel free to write to hr.dk@netcompany.com.

_All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

_

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment. Our recruitment processes are based on individual merit. If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support during the interview process, please email our recruiters at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com for assistance.

Head of Data Platform – build Gubra’s data foundation from the ground up

Do you want to build the data foundation behind scientific innovation in a growing biotech company? Gubra is looking for a Head of Data Platform to take end-to-end ownership of a new enterprise data platform connecting scientific, operational, and business data across the organisation.

The ambition is to create a scalable data foundation that supports research, laboratory operations, machine learning, and selected business functions across Gubra.

Build the platform – and the team around it

Gubra is investing in its digital and data foundation, and you will join at an early stage.

As Head of Data Platform, you will lead the design, implementation, and operation of the platform, built around AWS and Databricks. You will work across architecture, data pipelines, reusable data products, governance, and security while translating scientific and business needs into technical priorities.

At the same time, you will build and lead the data engineering team. Two Data Engineers are planned to join, an external Data Architect is already supporting the initial design, and the team is expected to grow further. You will report directly to the CTO and become part of the CTO’s leadership team.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Leading the design and development of a scalable and secure enterprise data platform

• Building reliable data pipelines and reusable data products for scientists, ML teams, engineers, and business users

• Defining the platform roadmap and driving key architectural and technical decisions

• Establishing data governance, security, access control, and documentation standards

• Building, mentoring, and developing the data engineering team

• Working closely with stakeholders across research, laboratory operations, software engineering, and the wider business.

Who are you?

You have a strong background in data engineering, analytics, or data platforms and experience leading both people and technical delivery. You combine leadership with enough technical depth to challenge architectural decisions and engage credibly with engineers.

You bring extensive experience with AWS and Databricks and have designed scalable, secure, and governed data solutions before. Experience with lakehouse architecture, data mesh, medallion architecture, Airflow, Delta Lake, or Unity Catalog is an advantage.

Experience from biotech, pharma, life sciences, or another research-intensive environment is beneficial but not required. The same applies to experience with regulated environments and GxP.

Personally, you are a pragmatic and collaborative leader who can create a clear direction, bring stakeholders and employees with you, and balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

About Gubra

Gubra is a purpose-driven biotech company where technology, data, and science come together to create life-changing therapies. The organisation combines Biotech, CRO, and Venture activities and brings scientists, engineers, and business teams together across the organisation.

Digital, Data & IT is strengthening the foundation beneath this work by connecting scientific, operational, and business data and enabling advanced analytics and machine learning.

Principal Enterprise Architect – shape the technology choices behind Gubra’s growth

Build, buy, integrate or simplify? As Gubra grows, so does the number and complexity of technology decisions across the organisation. Gubra is therefore looking for a Principal Enterprise Architect who can bring direction and coherence to its technology landscape.

In this newly established role, you will become a close architectural partner to the CTO and work across business, science, and technology. Your job is not to own one particular platform or technology. Instead, you will help Gubra make the right technology choices across scientific systems, enterprise applications, ERP, data, AI, cloud, and integrations.

Turn complex needs into pragmatic technology choices

As Principal Enterprise Architect, you will work closely with business leaders, scientists, Product Managers, and technology teams to understand what they are trying to achieve before translating those needs into architecture options and recommendations.

That could mean assessing whether to build a capability internally or invest in a SaaS platform. Another could involve defining how a new solution should integrate with Gubra’s existing landscape, exploring an AI opportunity, or helping a new venture establish a technology foundation that works today without limiting it tomorrow.

You will also help establish the architecture principles, standards, and guardrails that create consistency across Gubra. The ambition is not architecture for architecture’s sake, but enough direction to enable teams to make better decisions independently.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Advising on technology choices across enterprise applications, ERP, data, AI, cloud, security, and integrations

• Evaluating COTS and SaaS solutions and supporting build-vs-buy decisions

• Defining and evolving architecture principles, standards, and reusable patterns

• Translating business and scientific needs into pragmatic architecture recommendations

• Working with Software, Data, ML, Infrastructure, and Security teams to ensure decisions are technically viable

• Identifying opportunities for AI and modernisation across the organisation

• Following developments within AI, cloud, data sovereignty, and emerging technologies.

An architect who asks the right questions

You bring 5+ years of relevant experience as an Enterprise Architect, Principal Architect, or in a similar role, with broad experience across enterprise applications, data, cloud, integrations, security, and modern software platforms.

You understand ERP and enterprise business systems and how they connect to a broader technology landscape. You are comfortable discussing APIs, integration patterns, identity, security, cloud architecture, and data interoperability, and you have experience assessing COTS or SaaS platforms and making technology recommendations.

You also understand modern AI architecture and how AI capabilities can become part of real business workflows. Experience from pharma, biotech, life sciences, drug discovery, or another R&D-intensive environment is relevant, while experience with GxP is an advantage.

Just as importantly, you are curious enough to challenge the problem before proposing the solution. You can discuss opportunities with business leaders and scientists and then go into sufficient technical depth with engineers to make decisions credible and implementable.

You are comfortable influencing across teams without formal authority and know when architecture adds value – and when it simply adds another layer of complexity.

Where science, business and technology meet

Gubra is a purpose-driven biotech company where technology, data, and science come together to create life-changing therapies. Its activities span Biotech, CRO, and Venture, creating a technology landscape that needs to support different business models, scientific disciplines, and ways of working.

Digital, Data & IT works across these areas to create the digital foundation supporting both scientific innovation and business operations. As Principal Enterprise Architect, you will have a broad view across that landscape and help ensure technology decisions support where Gubra is going next.

The position is based at Gubra in Hørsholm, Denmark and reports directly to the CTO.

If you have any questions about the position, you are always welcome to contact Kathrine Schlegel Rasmussen at ksr@capaxrecruitment.com.

jobs.occupation: Computational and Data Staff Scientist Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Protein Design
jobs.description:
We seek an experienced, highly motivated, and independent computational and data scientist to support the Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Protein Design (CPD), University of Copenhagen (UCPH). The post suits someone with experience in computational chemistry, biology, and/or structural biology, as well as managing big data. This is a full-time position, starting 1 February 2027 and employment through 31 July 2032.

  Our research
 The CPD is a new initiative at UCPH. It is a multidisciplinary centre that works across the university—notably with the Departments of Biology, Drug Design and Pharmacology, Chemistry, and Computer Science—and with national and international academic and industrial partners. CPD is funded by an initial grant of 700M DKK for seven years from the Novo Nordisk Foundation. At capacity, the CPD is expected to have ≈8 research groups, ≈80 researchers, and support staff. Research will encompass the growing protein design landscape with computational, experimental, applied and hybrid projects.

  The CPD's vision and mission are to accelerate protein design by deepening understanding of sequence-to-structure/function relationships in proteins, and to train the next generation of protein scientists to apply protein-design approaches and methods to a diverse array of fundamental and real-world challenges.  

  CPD research is broadly organised into three themes: Programmable De Novo Protein Design, aimed at improving methods for protein design by combining rational, physics-based and AI-based approaches; Contextualised Protein Design, that is, designing proteins that are fit for purpose such as working directly and optimally in cells, chemical reactors, etc; and Biodesign for Sustainability and Healthcare, for instance working with biotech and industry to deliver synthetic proteins to address grand challenges in these areas.

  Data science at CPD: Increasingly, modern protein science is about data: collecting it, organising it, analysing it, and learning from it to build a deeper understanding of how proteins fold and function. Protein design is no different. Indeed, through the application of generative AI, it is at the leading edge of the confluence of data science and protein science. To coordinate this in the CPD, we are looking for someone experienced in and excited about working at this interface.

  Further information on the CPD see: cpd.ku.dk.

  Learn more about the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, https://drug.ku.dk/

  Your job
 Specifically, we seek a talented computational and data scientist and team player to help develop research infrastructure, including hardware and computational tools, to advance the CPD’s research and mission. jobs.description:
Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management and Department of Biology, invites applicants for three two-year Postdoc positions within forest microbiome manipulation. The positions are part of the project “MycoForest - Stimulating Forest carbon uptake and storage by mycorrhizal inoculation”, which is financed under the Innomission partnership INNO-CCUS by Innovation Fund Denmark.
 
 Start date is 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.
 
 The project
 The soil microbiome plays a crucial role in soil- and ecosystem functioning including ecosystem carbon sequestration and support of plant nutrient acquisition.
 
 Denmark is devoted to become carbon neutral by 2045/2050, a goal involving a significant role for biological carbon sequestration and storage. A part of the Danish strategy to reach carbon neutrality is to afforest former agricultural land thereby increasing biological ecosystem carbon capture and storage. However, agricultural soils do not harbor an optimal microbiome for initial tree growth and forest ecosystem development. This may lead to increased mortality, reduced tree growth and slower development of forest soil functions and ultimately non-optimal carbon capture, especially in the early stages of afforestation.
 
 Therefore, the MycoForest project aims to manipulate and assist the microbiome of agricultural soils through mycorrhizal inoculation as an integrated part of tree planting to stimulate tree growth and carbon sequestration. Therefore, MycoForest at University of Copenhagen is hiring three postdocs to become part of this novel journey towards increased biological carbon sequestration and to play key roles in the scientific investigations.
 
 Each of the three postdocs will cover one of three distinct areas of fundamental importance to understand and document the role of the microbiome in afforestation.
 
 The three key areas are:

   	
• Microbial and mycorrhizal fungal development 	
• Soil functioning and soil carbon dynamics 	
• Tree survival and growth, and carbon uptake   
 The studies will involve controlled greenhouse as well as field scale experiments, and the three postdocs will each be responsible for one of the three specific parts of the project. At the same time, they will be closely linked to each other through tight collaboration on establishment and sampling of the afforestation experiment. The postdoc positions will start as soon as possible and will run for 2 years. For the requirements of the specific postdocs, please see the descriptions below.
 
 Contact: Specific questions for each of the postdocs, please see below. For general MycoForest questions, please contact Claus Beier, cbe@ign.ku.dk.
 
 Postdoc 1 – Soil microbial development after mycorrhizal inoculation
 The post doc will oversee the formulation and addition of fungal or other types of inoculums and will follow and quantify the mycorrhizal fungal colonization of seedlings, root and soil. Experimentation will be both in mesocosm/greenhouse conditions and in the field. Colonization will be followed in different soils and host trees with a combination of classical microscopic techniques and novel molecular methods. The studies aim to document successful establishment of mycorrhizal fungi within the indigenous communities.
 
 Therefore, we are looking for candidates with specific knowledge and hands-on with:

   	
• Fungi in general including mycorrhizal fungi, preferentially ectomycorrhiza 	
• Field experience in general, handling and sorting soils and roots in specific 	
• Microscopy, especially stereo microscopy of roots 	
• DNA extraction og plants and soil and PCR optimizations including qPCR 	
• Bioinformatics and statistical analysis of meta-barcoding datasets   
 The post doc will work closely together with PD 2 and 3 for plant and soil responses to inoculations.
 
 Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Rasmus Kjøller, Department of Biology, rasmusk@bio.ku.dk, Phone: +45 35322311
 
 Postdoc 2 – Soil functioning and soil carbon dynamics in response to mycorrhizal inoculation
 The post doc will study effects of inoculation in different soil types and tree species on soil carbon processes including formation of persistent SOC fractions.  The postdoc will study soil carbon dynamics in mesocosm/greenhouse conditions in close cooperation with postdoc 1 and in field experimental conditions in cooperation with postdoc 3. The project will address how inoculation and changes in the mycorrhizal community composition will affect soil carbon sequestration processes in post-agricultural soils. The studies will shed light on the extent to which inoculation with forest-associated mycorrhiza and forest soil will change the soil C input quantity and quality from roots and microbial necromass, eventually enhancing accumulation of persistent forms of SOC. 
 
 We are looking for a candidate with a PhD in the fields of soil science and organic matter studies, soil ecology and biogeochemistry. Previous experience with plant-soil interactions in field, mesocosm and laboratory experiments using chemical soil analyses including soil organic carbon (organic matter fractionation and biomarkers targeting microbial and plant origin of organic matter), carbon isotopes, roots, and microbial taxonomic and functional community composition will be considered a plus.
 
 Principal supervisor is Professor Lars Vesterdal, Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, lv@ign.ku.dk, Phone: +45 61670865
 
 Postdoc 3 – Tree responses to mycorrhiza inoculation
 The postdoc will establish and follow field experiments in practical afforestation sites and monitor plant responses such as growth and survival, mycorrhizal colonization, and plant community development.
 
 The studies will address the potential of inoculation with forest-associated mycorrhiza and forest soil to stimulate survival, growth and carbon draw down of forest trees and communities including the role of tree species and soil type interactions. 
 
 We are looking for highly motivated candidates with a PhD in plant or forestry science and interest and experience in:

   	
• Afforestation, forestry and forest ecology 	
• Design and analysis of experiments 	
• Field work and practical application of technology in land management    
 Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Niclas Scott Bentsen, Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, nb@ign.ku.dk, Phone: +45 20206318.
 
 General qualifications
 Apart from the specific qualifications and interests listed above, we look for candidates with general competences in:

   	
• Driver license (mandatory) 	
• Handling of plants and soil 	
• Organizing and conducting field sampling 	
• Data management 	
• Statistics 	
• Scientific writing and publishing   
 Our groups and research – and what do we offer?
 The positions are located in three different groups at the university.
 
 Postdoc 1 is with Department of Biology, Fungal Ecology lab within Section of Terrestrial Ecology. The group works with/focuses on mycorrhizal fungal communities and their impact on ecosystem processes and plant health. We apply molecular markers to disentangle these otherwise invisible fungal populations and communities associated with plants and soil. Besides molecular markers, we also apply biochemical markers as well as classic microscopy and microbiological culturing of fungi. Another methodological strongpoint is various mesh-enclosure techniques to study and compartmentalize both the function and community composition of mycorrhizal fungal mycelia in soil.
 
 Postdoc 2 and 3 are with Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, one in the Biogeochemistry group and one in the Silviculture, Trees and Bioresources group. In the Biogeochemistry Group we are dedicated to improving the understanding of ecosystem functioning with particular focus on how ecosystems will respond to environmental changes and to management actions. We quantify the pools and fluxes of matter in semi-natural and managed ecosystems and measure the processes related to input and output fluxes in control of soil C stocks to answer questions such as “Can we sequester C in soils by afforestation of cropland soils, and how does this interact with the soil fauna and microbes when using certain tree species or tree species mixtures?” The Silviculture, Trees and Bioresources group encompas expertise in forestry, ecological restoration, growth modelling and systems analysis. The group is dedicated to advance the understanding, development, and management of forest ecosystems to support a wide range of ecosystem services, including carbon storage, material and energy provision, groundwater regulation, and biodiversity conservation.
 
 Department of Biology is located at Norre Campus and Department of Geosciences on Frederiksberg Campus, close to central Copenhagen. The departments offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environments. The departments are planning to increase their focus on the climate change mitigation potential of forests in upcoming projects. We therefore welcome applications from candidates with a broader interest in the intersection of forests, forest-based climate solutions, biosphere-atmosphere interaction, and related themes.
 
 Responsibilities and tasks

   	
• Carry out independent research projects under the PI’s supervision and in close collaboration with the other PostDocs and researchers within the MycoForest project. 	
• Report and disseminate the periodic progress and results 	
• Take part in relevant teaching activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at relevant journals 	
• Actively take part in the research environments at the departments, sections and within the project.   
 We are looking for the following further qualifications:

   	
• Strong ability to interpret data and think analytically, critically, and conceptually. 	
• Strong social competence including interpersonal skills, teamwork and networking ability, and presentation skills 	
• Strong personal competence including autonomy, goal-oriented mind-set, planning/organizing/prioritizing, perseverance, problem-solving skills 	
• General personal leadership skills including ability to translate long-term goals to daily work situations (strategic time managing); be flexible to adjust one’s own behavior and thinking according to the (relevant/local) context so as to attain the desired goals (learning ability) 	
• Good language skills and fluency in English   
 Terms of employment
 Employment is full-time and for 2 years.
 
 The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.
 
 Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.
 
 Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.
 
 You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).
 
 Application and Assessment Procedure
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and indicate which of the 3 positions you are applying for.
 
 The application is submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.
 
 Please include:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) – please relate how the above required abilities are represented in your past work experiences 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor’s or master’s and PhD and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list 	
• Reference letters (if available)   
 Application deadline:
 The deadline for applications is 29 October 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.
 
 We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.
 
 The further process
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.
 
 The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.
 
 Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in week 49-50 2026.
 
 Applicants must be prepared for further security screening related to international research collaborations as part of the recruitment process, when UCPH considers it appropriate from a holistic consideration
 
 Questions
 For specific information about the Postdoc position, please contact the principal supervisor.

jobs.description:
Are you interested in developing thin-film solar cells designed to operate efficiently under indoor lighting and thereby contributing to the green transition? 

At DTU Electro, you will have the opportunity to break new ground by harvesting energy from ambient light and help pave the way towards sustainable technologies.

The Thin-Film Photovoltaics Group at DTU Electro is seeking candidates for a PhD Scholarship focused on the development and characterization of highly efficient Sb₂S₃ solar cells. You will investigate materials, interfaces, and device architectures to understand and overcome the fundamental limitations of photovoltaic performance under low-light conditions.

The position is offered within the framework of DTU’s Alliances and Strategic Partnerships with Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech), Estonia. You will be part of an international research collaboration combining thin-film synthesis, solar-cell fabrication, advanced optoelectronic and defect characterization, and device testing under realistic illumination conditions. As part of the PhD project, you will undertake a research stay at TalTech and work closely with researchers from both universities.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The PhD project focuses on developing high-efficiency Sb₂S₃ thin-film solar cells for indoor energy harvesting. The project will investigate how material properties, interfaces, and device architecture influence charge transport, recombination, and voltage losses under low-intensity illumination. The overall objective is to develop solar cells optimized for indoor light and demonstrate series-connected mini-modules capable of powering battery-free IoT devices.

Your primary responsibilities include:

• Develop and optimize Sb₂S₃ thin-film solar cells by engineering device architectures and interfaces to enhance charge collection while minimizing recombination and voltage losses under indoor illumination.
• Characterize solar cells under different LED spectra, light intensities, and illumination conditions relevant to realistic indoor environments.
• Investigate defect states, interface recombination, and open-circuit voltage losses, including advanced electrical characterization during a research stay at TalTech.
• Develop and characterize series-connected indoor photovoltaic mini-modules for battery-free IoT applications.
• Supervise and contribute to MSc/BSc student projects.
• Document and disseminate the research through scientific publications and international conference contributions
You should have a strong academic background in physics, chemistry, materials science, nanotechnology, or a related field. Prior knowledge of semiconductor physics and photovoltaics, and experience with thin-film materials, solar-cell fabrication, optoelectronic characterization, or indoor photovoltaics, would be particularly valuable.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Electro

jobs.description:
A three-year position as a Postdoctoral researcher is now available at the Copenhagen Health Complexity Center, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen. The Postdoc’s employment is expected to start on 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  About the Center

  You will be employed at the Copenhagen Health Complexity Center, which aims to build a strong scientific foundation for understanding and acting on complex public-health challenges. The Center leverages multi-layered nationwide social and health data combined with an interdisciplinary fusion of methods spanning data science, epidemiology, ethnography, econometrics, and systems science. Our research focuses on the complex interplay of health, social, and environmental factors that shape individuals, families, and networks over time. We emphasise interdisciplinary collaboration, offering you an opportunity to actively engage as a collaborative partner in different projects depending on your interests and expertise. Learn more about the Center and our research, vision, and values here.

  About the Department 

  The Department of Public Health provides the scientific foundation for researchers and educators who aim to improve public health, both nationally and globally, and to create greater insight into the links between health, the individual, and society as well as the ethical, equity, and political implications. This is achieved through research, education, and engagement with stakeholders and the general public along with a broad multidisciplinary research agenda that addresses most aspects of public health at a high international level. More information about the Department of Public Health is available here.

  About the position 

  The position will be nested within the Child Health group at the Center, where we advance knowledge through a combination of research activities that leverage the Center’s data infrastructures and methodological expertise, and engagement with policymakers and practitioners. The Center has developed a strategic partnership with a Danish municipality – the Thriving Communities Lab – which offers a platform for connecting the scientific activities at the Center with real-world health promotion efforts. The focus of this partnership is to enhance the conditions for adolescents to thrive through a dynamic learning process that involves professionals across sectors in the municipality, the local government, and researchers, over a period of several years. One question we will explore is whether computational modelling can usefully bring together local knowledge, scientific evidence, the Center’s data resources, and insights emerging from practical interventions, and so strengthen this learning process. Your work as a postdoc will be anchored around this question. Our vision at the Center is to build on this experience to engage with more municipalities over time, addressing a variety of complex health challenges.

  As a Postdoc, your responsibilities will primarily consist of: 

   	
• Spearheading the development of a decision-support/scenario exploration tool that offers policymakers a way to visualize and simulate systemic effects of social investments and programmes, in close collaboration with our partners in the Thriving Communities Lab. 	
• Engaging with municipal collaborators within the Thriving Communities Lab to ensure a dynamic interplay between research activities and local efforts. 	
• Exploring multi-layered life-course data from the Danish Life Course Cohort (DANLIFE), augmented with local data from the municipal partner, to map the interrelated landscape of well-being among adolescents. 	
• Contributing to scientific publications and engage in the dissemination of research results related to these topics. 	
• Collaborating with researchers in the Center on interdisciplinary projects. 	
• Participating in research-based teaching at the Department of Public Health. 	
• Actively contributing to the development of organisational elements within the Center, such as network activities, website, outreach initiatives, social engagements, scientific meetings, and more.   Profile 

  We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic researcher with the following competences and experience:

   	
• You have a PhD degree in social science, economics, epidemiology, data science, complexity science, computational science, or other related sciences. 	
• You have experience with system dynamics modelling. Experience with agent-based modelling, social return on investment analysis or other analytical frameworks to model social and systemic impacts of social policies and programmes would also be an advantage. 	
• Experience working with Danish register data is an advantage. 	
• You are motivated to engage in participatory processes with practitioners and policymakers, and to collaborate with a variety of stakeholders to foster change. 	
• You have an active interest in complex-systems science applied to public health and epidemiology. 	
• You have proficient communication skills and a proven ability to work in interdisciplinary teams. 	
• You have excellent English skills, both written and spoken. 	
• Danish language skills are an advantage but not essential.   Place of employment

  The place of employment is the Copenhagen Health Complexity Center, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen, next to the Lakes in Central Copenhagen.

  Terms of employment 
 The average working hours are 37 hours per week. The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 3 years. The start date is February 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or another relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 35,000 DKK/approx. 4,700 EUR (October 2021 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 17.1 % to your pension fund. Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark for the past 10 years. The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2020.

  Further information

  For specific information about the position, please contact the Associate professor Christopher Jamil de Montgomery: cmon@sund.ku.dk

  Applicants may find the following links useful:

   	
• Copenhagen Health Complexity Center: https://healthcomplex.dk/ 	
• University of Copenhagen: http://ku.dk/english/ 	
• Department of Public Health: http://publichealth.ku.dk/ 	
• International Staff Mobility: https://ism.ku.dk/   Application process

  Your application should be written in English and must include the following documents – all in PDF format:

   	
• Letter of motivation (max 1 page). Please briefly describe your previous research experience and interests as well as what attracts you to the position. 	
• Curriculum Vitae, including a list of publications. 	
• Certified/signed copies of
 	a) PhD certificate (if the PhD has not been completed, a written statement from the applicant’s supervisor will suffice)
 	b) Master of Science certificate. 	
• A research plan (max 2 pages) outlining your ideas for how a decision-support/scenario exploration tool could be developed, drawing on system dynamics modelling or other analytical frameworks suitable for modelling dynamic effects of social policies and programmes.   Please submit your application by clicking on “Apply Now” below. Only online applications will be considered.

  After the expiration of the deadline for applications, the authorised recruitment manager will select applicants for assessment based on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been advanced for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment has been completed, each applicant is given an opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant themselves.

  You can read more about the recruitment process here: https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  Application deadline 

  Deadline for applications: 31/10/2026 23.59pm CET 

  We reserve the right to reject material received after the deadline, and to reject applications that do not meet the abovementioned requirements.

  Interviews are expected to be held in week 47-48.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of their personal background.
